newsitem.title: UK: N.Irish prisoners moved out of prison secure units.
newsitem.headline: N.Irish prisoners moved out of prison secure units.

text.p: Thirteen prisoners convicted of guerrilla offences relating to Northern Ireland have been moved out of special secure units in British prisons following a review of their status, the Prison Service said on Tuesday.
A spokesman said the 13, who have been moved to normal cells within their high security jails, were now regarded as "high risk" rather than "exceptional risk" prisoners.

Asked whether the move was related to the renewed ceasefire called by the Irish Republican Army on July 20, the spokesman said: "It is merely a reclassification which reflected the latest security situation."

He said there was no question of the prisoners being transferred to other jails. The IRA and its political wing Sinn Fein have called for guerrilla prisoners to be moved to Northern Irish jails, making it easier for their families to visit them.
The spokesman did not name the prisoners involved. He said the status of one other prisoner, with no connection with guerrilla offences, had been similarly changed.
